objective: The coordinator's pick of 2026-11-26 after LAYERS-20261126-001, on the owner's question whether recursion exists: the second-check study's exchange (each shortest allowed change of a grown stage read as a knot, loose values pinned) gives the bare ring back from the ring grown one round; does it do so for other starts (trees, several rings, sampled starts), under both knot laws; is grow-then-exchange a return to the same start, to another start, or a cycle; and can growth supply the pinning, or is it always ours? title: Recursion's lead: does growing and then exchanging give a start back?
